content.title: What time is NY Mets vs Cardinals series finale? How to watch today
content.text: Updated April 1, 2026, 1:41 p.m. ETThe New York Mets (3-2, second in NL East) finish up a three-game series against the St. Louis Cardinals (3-2, second in NL Central) on Wednesday afternoon.The Mets offense couldn't get anything going at the plate on Tuesday night, as they were shutout for the first time this season and recorded only three hits in a 3-0 loss against the Cardinals.Despite the defeat, Mets starting pitcher Kodai Senga was one of the lone positives for the team on Tuesday night, as he struck out nine and gave up two runs in six innings but failed to get any run support from an offense that had one extra-base hit, a Juan Soto double in the sixth inning.The Mets will need to win the rubber match in St. Louis on Wednesday to secure a second consecutive series victory to begin the season.The Mets-Cardinals series finale is currently in a rain delay, with first pitch slated for 2:15 p.m. ET.The Mets road trip continues as they'll head to the Bay Area for a four-game set versus the San Francisco Giants.Here's how to watch, the starting pitchers for both organizations and our prediction on who will win the Mets vs. Cardinals series finale on Wednesday:When is NY Mets vs Cardinals game today?Date: Wednesday, April 1What time is NY Mets vs Cardinals first pitch today?Time: 2:15 p.m. ETThe Mets have announced that first pitch is expected for 2:15 p.m. following the rain delay.How to watch NY Mets vs Cardinals game todayTV channel: SNYHow to stream NY Mets vs Cardinals game todayStreaming: MLB.TV for out of market viewersNY Mets, Cardinals starting pitchers todayMets: Freddy Peralta (1-0, 7.20 ERA)Cardinals: Matthew Liberatore (0-0, 1.80 ERA)Freddy Peralta looks to bounce back in his second start with the Mets. Peralta, who started on Opening Day for the Mets, did strike out seven batters but surrendered four runs and six hits in five innings of work. The two-time All-Star still earned the victory thanks to the Mets first-inning offensive explosion, where they scored five runs alone in the first in a 11-7 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates on March 26 at Citi Field.Matthew Liberatore was the Opening Day starter for the Cardinals. The 26-year-old southpaw earned a no-decision after he pitched five innings and conceded one run on seven hits.NY Mets vs Cardinals game oddsOdds according to BetMGM as of Wednesday, April 1:Spread: Mets by 1.5Over/under: 8Moneyline: Mets (-170), Cardinals (+140)Will Mets beat Cardinals today? Our predictionThe starting pitching advantage is noticeable in the series finale, with Freddy Peralta having a much better second outing as he strikes out eight hitters and allows one run as the Mets offense does plenty to give Peralta his second victory in as many starts and the series win over the Cardinals as they look ahead to San Francisco.Prediction: Mets 6, Cardinals 2
